Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Monica Desai, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Monica Desai, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Johnson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Alex.

Alex Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Monica. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our revenue reached a record $19.8 billion, representing a robust 23% year-over-year increase and exceeding our previously issued guidance by a significant $800 million. This exceptional performance was primarily fueled by sustained and accelerating demand within our Data Center Group (DCG), coupled with a surprisingly resilient PC-centric (PCG) performance despite anticipated macroeconomic headwinds. We believe this strong start to the year positions us favorably to achieve our full-year targets and underscores the effectiveness of our strategic investments in key growth areas. This reflects the strength of our product portfolio and the effectiveness of our strategic investments.

We also continued to drive improvements through our gross margin performance. Our Q1 gross margin came in at 62.0%, exceeding both our internal expectations and the guidance provided during our Q4 2023 earnings call. This positive outcome is primarily attributable to the robust flow-through of higher platform revenue. However, this positive impact was partially offset by specific headwinds related to our memory business and the strategic divestiture of our Home Gateway Business, which is allowing us to focus on higher-growth areas.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our CapEx guidance. Intel is currently refraining from providing formal, full-year CapEx guidance due to the persistent macroeconomic uncertainties stemming from the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic's fluctuating impact on supply chains, construction timelines, and overall demand makes accurate long-term forecasting exceedingly difficult. However, management has offered crucial insights into specific areas that warrant closer examination, where we’ve prioritized investments in advanced node technologies.

Now I’ll hand it over to Sarah to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our Data Center Group delivered a stellar performance in the last fiscal year, achieving $7 billion in revenue, representing a robust 43% year-over-year growth. This impressive growth was fueled by strong demand across all key sub-segments, reflecting the increasing adoption of cloud computing, the ongoing digital transformation initiatives within enterprises, and the expanding needs of communication service providers has contributed meaningfully to our overall success.

Second, we saw positive contribution from the Client Computing Group (CCG) as well. The Client Computing Group (CCG) reported revenue of $9.8 billion, marking a 14% year-over-year increase. This growth was primarily driven by the continued strength of the notebook market and higher modem sales, reflecting the ongoing shift towards remote work and online learning, which helped us to achieve impressive results.

And although still early, our Q2 P&L guidance is promising. Our analysis of StellarTech's Q2 2024 guidance, which projects revenue of $18.5 billion and gross margins of approximately 56%, requires a deeper examination beyond the headline figures. The projected revenue represents a slight (approximately 3%) decrease year-over-year compared to the $19.1 billion reported in Q2 2023. However, it's crucial to understand the drivers behind this anticipated performance and the significant sequential margin compression, is showing positive momentum.

With that, I’ll turn it to David for a deeper look at operational performance.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was the CapEx spend. During the second quarter of FY2023, Intel's CapEx spend was approximately $6.2 billion, which is a 12% decrease compared to the $7.0 billion spent in Q2 of FY2022. This decrease is primarily attributable to the regulatory delays, particularly in North America and Europe.

Additionally, the Client Computing Group’s operating margin improved significantly to 43%, up 7 percentage points year-over-year. This margin expansion was driven by a combination of factors, including:
Higher Average Selling Prices (ASPs): Increased demand for premium notebooks and high-performance processors led to higher ASPs, boosting profitability.
Improved Product Mix: The shift towards higher-margin products, such as premium notebooks and 5G modems, contributed to the margin expansion.
Operational Efficiencies: Ongoing efforts to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce operating costs also played a role has enabled more efficient operations.

We’re also seeing early traction in our efforts to mitigate the gross margin pressures we are facing. We are taking the following actions:
Negotiating Long-Term Supply Contracts: We are actively negotiating long-term supply contracts with key raw material suppliers to mitigate the impact of price volatility.
Product Innovation and Cost Optimization: We are accelerating our efforts to develop more cost-effective manufacturing processes and innovative product designs that reduce reliance on expensive raw materials.
Pricing Strategy Adjustments: We are carefully evaluating our pricing strategy to ensure that we are appropriately reflecting the value of our products and services while remaining competitive in the market, where updated processes and strategic adjustments are starting to yield positive results.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily for the tech and product update.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, David.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to our gross margin improvement, which are due to a decrease in promotional activities. In Q4, we had launched a significant campaign to drive usage on our newly launched cloud platform "Synergy". This campaign included upfront discounts and promotional pricing to onboard new customers and drive utilization. As these pricing promotions were rolled back in Q1, we saw a significant improvement in our margins, supporting broader adoption and improved profitability.

We’ve also made significant strides in supporting our Q2 P&L guidance. The projected 56% gross margin represents a substantial 6-point sequential decline from the 62% reported in Q1 2024. This compression is a significant concern and requires a detailed explanation. One of the reasons for this is factory underutilization. Intel's ongoing efforts to ramp up advanced manufacturing nodes (Intel 4 and Intel 3) and expand overall capacity are leading to temporary factory underutilization. This negatively impacts gross margins due to fixed costs being spread across a smaller production volume, and our teams are working tirelessly to address these issues.

And finally, on the efforts to mitigate the gross margin pressures, we are actively negotiating long-term supply contracts with key raw material suppliers to mitigate the impact of price volatility. We are also accelerating our efforts to develop more cost-effective manufacturing processes and innovative product designs that reduce reliance on expensive raw materials. For example, we are exploring the use of sodium-ion batteries as an alternative to lithium-ion batteries. Our new architecture is geared towards long-term cost optimization.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the CapEx guidance and whether you foresee any further regulatory delays?

Alex Johnson:
Yes, we do anticipate a slight shift in the timing of certain capital expenditures. Specifically, the company expects a portion of its planned investments to be pushed out of the current fiscal year (FY2023, assuming this is the current period) due to unforeseen regulatory approval delays. Our internal models estimate that approximately $1.8 billion (representing roughly 7% of the originally planned $25.7 billion total CapEx for the year) may be deferred into the first half of the following fiscal year (FY2024). This delay is primarily attributed to construction permit approvals for the expansion of the Fab 52 facility in Arizona and, to a lesser extent, environmental impact assessments for the new chip packaging facility in Malaysia. While we are working closely with regulators, further delays are possible but not anticipated.

Analyst 2:
On the Data Center Group performance, how much of the growth was attributable to increased volume versus increased pricing?

Sarah Chen:
Within our Data Center Group, server revenue witnessed a 38% YoY increase to $7.5 billion, driven by both volume and average selling price (ASP) increases. Hyperscale customers continued to be a major contributor, accounting for approximately 45% of the server revenue, showing a 42% increase compared to Q1 last year. Strong adoption of our 4th Generation Xeon Scalable processors, codenamed "Sapphire Rapids," fueled ASP growth within this segment. We estimate that Sapphire Rapids contributed approximately $2.8 billion to the overall server revenue this quarter. So, it was a combination of both, with ASPs playing a significant role.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to gross margin improvements?

Emily Carter:
Certainly. The implementation of advanced automation technologies in our Asian manufacturing facilities, particularly in Malaysia, led to a reduction in direct labor costs and improved throughput, contributing approximately 50 basis points to the YoY gross margin improvement. We also experienced a favorable pricing environment for certain key components, notably NAND flash memory, due to industry-wide oversupply in the latter half of 2023. This allowed us to reduce our cost of goods sold (COGS) in some product lines, further supporting the gross margin expansion. We are continuing to refine these initiatives for further gains.

Analyst 4:
And finally, regarding the operating margin, is the anticipated improvement in Q3 sustainable in the long term?

David Lee:
Looking ahead to Q3, we anticipate continued revenue growth and expect our operating margin to be in the range of 30.5% to 31.5%. This forecast reflects our expectation of continued strong demand, the benefits of our cost-saving initiatives, and a gradual easing of raw material cost pressures. We will continue to closely monitor the market environment and adjust our strategies as needed to maximize profitability and shareholder value. It is our intention to sustain these improvements through a combination of cost control and revenue growth.

Closing

Alex Johnson:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
